candidates.explanation: When no user matches the social id but a user exists with the same email, the code takes over that account. If the account is not inactive, i.e. it is active, it overwrites user.provider with the social provider (google) and sets user.socialId, then saves it. A confirmed, active email/password account therefore becomes a google account. The email login then rejects it with 'needLoginViaProvider:google'. The status check is the wrong way round. It modifies active accounts and leaves inactive ones alone.

fix.description: Do not rewrite provider/socialId on an existing email account. Use the existing user as is, or reject with a conflict error when the provider differs. Remove the update block, or at least don't change provider for active accounts.
